artifacts.summary: Full A-I follow-up task specification (dependencies, file_scope) plus a per-task reconciliation table for every collision named in the dispatch, with the A/B ordering wrinkle resolved (no dependency edge) and the specs/ disposition flagged as a user decision.

next_steps: Run /plan 629 to turn the A-I task specification and the reconciliation table into concrete task-creation and task-revision steps against specs/state.json.

user_decision.question: At the publication gate (task H, Phase 8), how should specs/ be disposed of: untrack it (default), keep it permanently published, or move it to an unpublished branch before the gate?
options: Untrack specs/ (and CLAUDE.md, .claude-extensions.json, .syncprotect, .gitattributes) in one commit at the publication gate, per PUBLICATION_REFACTOR.md Section 8
Keep specs/ tracked and published permanently
Move specs/ to a separate unpublished branch before the gate, preserving full provenance outside the published history
user_decision.recommended: Untrack specs/ (and CLAUDE.md, .claude-extensions.json, .syncprotect, .gitattributes) in one commit at the publication gate, per PUBLICATION_REFACTOR.md Section 8

memory_candidates.content: When reconciling a large, document-driven task-set-creation programme (e.g. a publication refactor with Section 9 paste-ready follow-ups) against dozens of pre-existing open tasks, checking each named collision against the actual current file_scope/description text (not the summarizing dispatch prose) frequently resolves an apparent conflict as already moot (e.g. a file the new task 'untracks' turning out to already be empty and fully handled by the colliding task's completed phase) or as requiring only a scheduling note rather than a hard dependency edge (e.g. sequencing after in-flight partial-status tasks without literally blocking on them).

An ADR's own prose can directly resolve a stated 'ordering wrinkle' in a companion programme document: ADR-010 explicitly disclaimed that the Boneyard-relocation decision 'does not depend on' the frozen-LaTeX-retirement phase, which settled whether two bundled follow-up tasks (A = phases 0+2, B = phase 1, with B nominally sitting between A's two halves per the document's stated 0->1->2 chain) needed a dependency edge. Cross-referencing the ADR against the phase document is worth doing before assuming the document's default linear order is load-bearing.
